title: Joining the Sounds: Ready for Level 1
overview:
Join the sounds into words.
b-u-s makes bus.
Read your first sentences.
Then go to Level 1.
functions: Join sounds together to read a short word
Read a short sentence you know by ear
Find the first, middle and last sound in a word
Say when a try was right or wrong
Read a sentence out loud with a full stop
Say you are ready for Level 1
learningPath: Words: joining, and your first sentences.
Patterns: blending, and the full stop.
Practice and quiz. Then go to Level 1.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 16. The last unit of Intro.
In Unit 2 you copied the shapes.
In Unit 3 you learned their names.
Today you join them and read.
Every letter has a sound.
b makes buh. u makes uh. s makes sss.
Now join them slowly.
buh ... uh ... sss.
Faster. b-u-s. Bus.
You just read a word.
Try another. m-a-p. Map.
And c-u-p. Cup.
That is all reading is. Joining sounds.
Now a whole sentence.
The man has a big bag.
Read it slowly, word by word.
The. Man. Has. A. Big. Bag.
Now again, faster.
The man has a big bag.
See the dot at the end? That is a full stop.
It says: this sentence is finished. Stop.
Your voice goes down at a full stop.
Now, about mistakes.
You will get words wrong. Everybody does.
A wrong try is not a bad thing.
Try, check, try again. That is how it works.
Last. You are ready for Level 1 now.
Level 1 Unit 0 does the letters again.
For you it will be easy. That is good.
Well done. Go on to Level 1.

grammar.title: Joining the sounds
grammar.explanation:
This is reading.
Everything before today was getting ready for it.
Slow first. Fast later.
grammar.rule:
b - u - s      →  bus
m - a - p      →  map
c - u - p      →  cup
s - i - t      →  sit
h - a - t      →  hat

Say each sound. Then say them together.
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word map.
1. First sound: m. Say it: mmm.
2. Middle sound: a. Say it: aaa.
3. Last sound: p.
4. Now join them slowly: mmm-aaa-p.
5. Now faster: map. You read it.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say the letter NAMES when you blend.
Not em-ay-pee. That makes no word.
Say the SOUNDS: mmm-aaa-p.
grammar.tip: Sounds, not names, when you read.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. b-u-s
2. m-a-p
3. c-u-p
4. s-i-t
5. h-a-t
6. b-e-d
grammar.answers:
1. bus
2. map
3. cup
4. sit
5. hat
6. bed
Five or six right? You can read. That is the whole point of this level.

grammar.title: First, middle, last
grammar.explanation:
Every short word has three parts.
Hearing them is what makes blending work.
grammar.rule:
bus:   first b   middle u   last s
map:   first m   middle a   last p
cup:   first c   middle u   last p

The middle sound is usually a, e, i, o or u.
grammar.workedExample:
You hear the word hat.
1. What do you hear first? h.
2. What is in the middle? a.
3. What is at the end? t.
4. Say them in order: h-a-t.
5. Now write it: hat.
grammar.mistake:
The middle sound is the hardest to hear.
It is almost always a, e, i, o or u.
If you are stuck, try those five.
grammar.tip: The middle is a vowel: a, e, i, o, u.
grammar.practice:
What is the FIRST sound?
1. bus
2. map
3. cup
What is the LAST sound?
4. bus
5. map
6. cup
grammar.answers:
1. b
2. m
3. c
4. s
5. p
6. p
Five or six right? You can take a word apart.

grammar.title: A sentence and its full stop
grammar.explanation:
A sentence says one whole thing.
It starts with a capital and ends with a dot.
grammar.rule:
The man has a big bag.
^                      ^
capital              full stop

The bus is here.
I have a cup.
My bag is big.
grammar.workedExample:
You write about a man with a bag.
1. Start with a capital letter: The.
2. Write the words in order.
3. At the end, put a dot.
4. That dot is the full stop.
5. Check: capital at the start, dot at the end.
grammar.mistake:
With no full stop, it runs into the next one.
The reader cannot tell where it ends.
grammar.tip: Capital at the start. Full stop at the end.
grammar.practice:
Write right or wrong.
1. The man has a big bag.
2. the bus is here.
3. I have a cup
4. My bag is big.
5. the cup is hot
grammar.answers:
1. right
2. wrong — no capital
3. wrong — no full stop
4. right
5. wrong — neither
Four or five right? You can write a sentence now.

grammar.title: Try, check, try again
grammar.explanation:
You will read words wrong. Everybody does.
A wrong try is part of reading, not a failure.
grammar.rule:
Try:        you say a word
Check:      you look, or you ask
Try again:  you say it better

Wrong is not bad.
Wrong and then right is learning.
grammar.workedExample:
You read bed as bad.
1. That is a wrong try. Fine.
2. Look at the middle letter again: e.
3. The e sound is eh, not aa.
4. Try again: b-e-d. Bed.
5. Right on the second try is a success.
grammar.mistake:
Do not stop at the first wrong try.
Almost nobody reads a new word right the first time.
grammar.practice:
What do you do?
1. You read it and it makes no word. ___
2. You are not sure of the middle sound. ___
3. You got it right. ___
4. You got it wrong two times. ___
grammar.answers:
1. Try again, slower.
2. Try a, e, i, o and u.
3. Say well done, and read the next one.
4. Ask somebody, then try again.
All four? You know how to keep going on your own.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Join the sounds
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each sound. Then join them.
1. b - u - s
2. m - a - p
3. c - u - p
4. s - i - t
5. h - a - t
6. b - e - d
Say the sounds, not the letter names.
Tap the mic. Say each word twice: slow, then fast.
Check: bus, map, cup, sit, hat, bed.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three sounds. Join them and say the word.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Read a sentence
speaking.instructions:
Read each sentence out loud.
Word by word first. Then again, faster.
1. The man has a big bag.
2. The bus is late.
3. The cup is not hot.
4. My bag is red.
5. I can read it.
Tap the mic. Read all five.
Check: did your voice go down at each full stop?
speaking.tutor: Read one sentence to the tutor. Ask if it was clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — First, middle, last
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Say the FIRST sound.
1. bus
2. map
3. cup
Now say the LAST sound.
4. bus
5. map
6. cup
Tap the mic. Say six sounds.
Check: b, m, c, s, p, p.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a short word. Say its first and last sound.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Read the signs
speaking.instructions:
Read each sign out loud.
Join the sounds if you need to.
STOP
BUS
EXIT
OPEN
SIT HERE
Tap the mic. Read all five.
Check: five signs read? Any you had to try twice?
Trying twice is fine. That is how reading works.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a sign you might see in a street.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — What I can do now
speaking.instructions:
Say five lines about this level.
1. I can say the alphabet.
2. I can write my name.
3. I can count to twenty.
4. I can read a short word.
5. I am ready for Level 1.
Tap the mic. Say the five lines.
Tap again. Listen back.
This is your record of finishing Intro. Keep it.
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor three things you can do now. Ask what Level 1 teaches.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Slow, then faster
speaking.instructions:
Read this sentence three times.
The man has a big bag.
First: word by word, very slow.
Second: a little faster.
Third: as one sentence. Your voice goes down.
Tap the mic. Read it three times.
Check: was the third one easier than the first?
speaking.tutor: Read the sentence to the tutor three times. Ask which was best.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Two sentences
writing.prompt:
Write two sentences.
Each one starts with a capital.
Each one ends with a full stop.
writing.model:
The man has a big bag.
My bag is red.
writing.criteria:
Two sentences.
A capital at the start of each.
A full stop at the end of each.
The words are in the right order.
writing.support: Write one sentence only. Copy it from the model.
writing.extension: Write a third sentence about yourself.

writing.title: Writing 2 — What I can do now
writing.prompt:
Write four lines.
Say four things you can do after this level.
Start each one with I can.
writing.model:
I can say the alphabet.
I can write my name.
I can count to twenty.
I can read a short word.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
I can at the start of each one.
A capital at the start. A full stop at the end.
They are all true.
writing.extension: Add one line: I am ready for Level 1.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Join and read
activities.instructions:
Join the sounds. Write the word.
1. b-u-s
2. m-a-p
3. c-u-p
4. s-i-t
5. h-a-t
6. b-e-d
7. p-e-n
8. b-a-g
activities.answers:
1. bus
2. map
3. cup
4. sit
5. hat
6. bed
7. pen
8. bag
Six or more right: you can read. That is this level's whole job.
Below six: say each sound out loud before you join them.
activities.solo: Say each one out loud, then write it.

activities.title: Practice 2 — First or last?
activities.instructions:
Write the sound.
1. The first sound in bus. ___
2. The first sound in map. ___
3. The last sound in cup. ___
4. The last sound in sit. ___
5. The middle sound in bus. ___
6. The middle sound in map. ___
activities.answers:
1. b
2. m
3. p
4. t
5. u
6. a
Five or six right: good. The middle is always a vowel.
activities.solo: Say each word out loud before you answer.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Read them out loud
activities.instructions:
Read each sentence out loud, twice.
1. The man has a big bag.
2. The bus is late.
3. The cup is not hot.
4. My bag is red.
5. I can read it.
activities.answers:
There is no written key.
Check: did you read all five?
Did your voice go down at each full stop?
Was the second reading easier than the first?
activities.solo: Record all five, then listen back once.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Right or wrong?
activities.instructions:
Is the sentence written correctly?
1. The man has a big bag.
2. the bus is here.
3. I have a cup
4. My bag is big.
5. the cup is hot
activities.answers:
1. right
2. wrong, no capital
3. wrong, no full stop
4. right
5. wrong, neither
Four or five right: you know what a sentence needs.

activities.title: Practice 5 — What do you do?
activities.instructions:
Choose what to do.
1. You read it and it makes no word. ___
2. You are not sure of the middle sound. ___
3. You got it right. ___
4. You got it wrong two times. ___
5. The word is long. ___
activities.answers:
1. Try again, slower.
2. Try a, e, i, o and u.
3. Read the next one.
4. Ask somebody, then try again.
5. Read it in two parts.
Four or five right: you can keep going on your own.
activities.solo: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Ready for Level 1?
activities.instructions:
Check yourself. Answer yes or no.
1. Can you say the alphabet?
2. Can you write your name?
3. Can you count to twenty?
4. Can you read bus, map and cup?
5. Can you say where it hurts?
6. Can you ask the way?
activities.answers:
Any true answer is right.
Four or more yes: go to Level 1 now.
Below four: do those units again first. There is no hurry.
Level 1 Unit 0 does the letters again, so you will meet them twice.
activities.solo: Answer honestly. This one is for you, not for a mark.

quizzes.q: When you read, you say the ___.
quizzes.why: Em-ay-pee makes no word. Mmm-aaa-p makes map.

quizzes.q: What is the first sound in cup?
The middle sound of a short word is usually ___.
quizzes.why: It is almost always a, e, i, o or u.

quizzes.q: What goes at the end of a sentence?
quizzes.why: A full stop says the sentence is finished.

quizzes.q: What goes at the start of a sentence?
quizzes.why: Every sentence starts with a capital.

quizzes.q: You read a word wrong. What do you do?
quizzes.why: Almost nobody reads a new word right the first time.

quizzes.q: A mistake when you are reading is ___.
quizzes.why: Wrong and then right is learning.

quizzes.q: What comes after the Intro level?
quizzes.why: Intro is the first level. Level 1 comes next.

quizzes.q: Level 1 Unit 0 teaches the letters again. For you that will be ___.
quizzes.why: You have done two units on the letters already.

quizzes.q: You have finished this level. What do you say to yourself?
quizzes.why: You say well done for a thing done well.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: This is the unit the level exists for
teacherNotes.note: Units 2 and 3 taught the shapes and then the names. Blending is where those two become reading. If a learner gets nothing else from Intro, they should leave able to sound out bus, map and cup.
Em-ay-pee will never make map, and a learner who has just spent Unit 3 learning the names will reach for them. Say the difference out loud at the start and expect to say it again.

teacherNotes.type: Mistakes need naming as normal, out loud
teacherNotes.note: An adult who reads a word wrong in front of another adult often stops trying. Pattern 4 exists for that, not for the technique. Say plainly that nobody reads a new word right the first time — it changes what the learner does next.

Level 1 Unit 0 teaches the letters and blending again, and its own overview offers a fast exit to Unit 1 for a learner who can already read bus, map and stop. An Intro graduate should take that exit. A learner who cannot yet should stay, and Practice 6 tells them so in as many words.

assignment.title: Read it, and go on to Level 1
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Read these words: bus, map, cup, sit, bed.
Say the sounds first, then the word.
Then read: The man has a big bag.
Then say: I am ready for Level 1.
2. Write two sentences. A capital at the start, a full stop at the end.
Listen back before you finish. Keep this recording.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
